label: conj:nuclear-knot-classification
title: Nuclear knot classification: braid closure type determines binding scale
html:
The closure of the nuclear braid \mathcal{N}(Z,N) in H_3(R, q) determines a bulk modification factor a(\mathcal{N}) for the BW binding energy. This factor is a single product over independent nucleon pairs:

  a(\mathcal{N})
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=1}^{n_{\mathrm{pairs}}}
    (1 - \varepsilon_i)

where \varepsilon_i is the Frobenius norm deviation of the i-th nucleon pair from the identity braid:

  • Amphicheiral pair (pp or nn in \mathcal{B}_3): \varepsilon = h^2 = (q - q^{-1})^2
  • Chiral pair (pn): \varepsilon = -h = -(q - q^{-1})

The sign convention: amphicheiral pairs (K = \bar{K}) deviate quadratically (h^2 > 0, reducing binding); chiral pairs deviate linearly (-h < 0, increasing binding).

A Pairs Deviations \varepsilon_i a(\mathcal{N})
1 0 — free nucleon
2 1 pn (chiral) -h 1 + h \approx 1.209
3 1 pp or nn (amphicheiral) h^2 1 - h^2 \approx 0.956
4 2 (pp + nn, amphicheiral) h^2, h^2 (1 - h^2)^2 \approx 0.914
\geq 5 many not derived not derived

The large-A limit is not derived. For fixed h \neq 0 and n amphicheiral pairs the product is (1 - h^2)^n, which tends to 0, not to 1, as n \to \infty (at q_0, h^2 \approx 0.044 gives (1 - h^2)^{n} < 1/2 once n \geq 16). So the pair product does not by itself recover the standard BW formula for heavy nuclei.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
